thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1: sustained queue growth and elevated tail latency for gpu-pool-prod. Customers hitting timeouts. Paging oncall. svc: /v1/generate, affected models: redwood-7b-quant, approx 30% of requests erroring or timing out. Root metrics: queue_depth, pod_ready=false, warmup_pending. See logs: https://internal.monitoring/redwood/incidents/1917654321

alex: acked. I'm on it, joining incident bridge. quick questions: is this multi-region?

priya: single region (us-west2) — traffic concentrated on the hot partition.

matt: looking at autoscaler. HPA metric `queue_length` spiked from 300 -> 2200 in ~45s but desired replicas only moved +2 due to max-surge controls. cooldown window is 4m.

alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) force scale gpu-pool-prod +6 replicas 2) temporarily lower HPA scale-down and cooldown 3) enable fallback model pool (cpu-backed) for small requests. doing 1 now.

matt: I ran `k8s scale` to bump desired -> 18. logs show provisioning jobs started but many pods stuck at ContainerCreating: image pull backoff for `prewarm-init`

ying: that matches warmup failures — registry auth started returning 401s at ~1917654270. pushing to infra to fix registry creds.

priya: customer-impact note: CS reports several timed-out requests from major customer acme-inc. Sarah, can you confirm severity/contacting?

sarah: on it. I've opened a priority ticket with account team and sent outage note to acme-inc. They're seeing ~40% error rate on batch runs. will update after next call.

alex: sharing quick log snippet for timeline and hypothesis building:
```
2026-03-15T03:45:06Z autoscaler controller: queue_length=312 -> 2234 (45s)
2026-03-15T03:45:12Z hpa: Desired=12 Current=10 MaxSurgePolicy=+2 cooldown=240s
2026-03-15T03:46:02Z kubelet: Pulling image prewarm-init:v1.2.1 -> 401 Unauthorized
2026-03-15T03:46:15Z pod: ContainerCreating -> CrashLoopBackOff prewarm-init
2026-03-15T03:47:00Z inference-runtime: fallback to small-models triggered for 8% requests
```

matt: hypothesis 1: registry auth flake prevented prewarm containers from coming up quickly, so even though HPA increased desired replicas, pods were NotReady and queue kept growing. hypothesis 2: HPA conservative surge policy + cooldown prevented aggressive scaling for bursty queue spikes.

ying: confirm — registry tokens rotated Friday and rollout may have missed some worker tokens. infra rolling a creds patch now.

priya: mitigation steps being executed: 1) infra patching registry creds 2) matt forced scale to ensure some pods get through once image pull fixed 3) alex toggled HPA policy to allow quicker surge (temp policy: maxSurge +6, cooldown 30s) 4) enable model-fallback route for low-latency clients.

alex: implementing step 3 now. matt please keep an eye on pod readiness and share `kubectl get pods -o wide` every 30s.

matt: copy. current pod states:
```
NAME                          READY  STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
gpu-pool-prod-1              1/1    Running            0          12m
gpu-pool-prod-2              0/1    ContainerCreating  0          2m
gpu-pool-prod-3              0/1    ImagePullBackOff    0          1m
gpu-pool-prod-4              0/1    Init:CrashLoopBackOff 3      45s
```

alex: warmup lag tracker: mark hypothesis A: registry creds -> warmup failures -> NotReady -> queue growth. Hypothesis B: HPA policy/cooldown + queue spike pattern caused underprovisioning independent of registry. We'll test by removing cooldown and observing scaler compute response.

ying: infra creds patch applied at 1917654605, image pulls started returning 200 after ~30s.

matt: pods now healthy: 14/18 ready at 1917654710. tail latency dropping.

priya: timeline so far:
- 1917654270: registry auth errors begin
- 1917654321: incident page (thread root)
- 1917654350: queue depth spike begins
- 1917654398: HPA limits hit (maxSurge)
- 1917654460: manual scale +6 requested
- 1917654605: infra creds patch applied
- 1917654710: pods stabilized 14/18 ready
- 1917654980: customer error rate dropped below 5%

alex: moving to handoff in 10m. Jordan, you'll take the post-incident RCA and own follow-ups: verify HPA surge policy is appropriate for queue spike distributions, add warmup preflight checks, and add alerting for registry auth failures tied to warmup. I'm putting a checklist below for the RCA.

jordan: taking handoff. checklist items I have so far (will expand):
- gather full autoscaler event logs and tuning history (last 7 days)
- correlate queue_depth distribution with request arrival patterns
- evaluate changing default HPA maxSurge from +2 -> +6 for gpu pools (with cost assessment)
- surface reg cred rotation playbook gaps and add healthcheck for prewarm image pulls
- follow up with CS for customer remediation notes and SLA credit if needed

sarah: I'll keep acme-inc updated. they requested an internal postmortem. please tag me when RCA draft is ready.

alex: final note in-thread: incident mitigated, customer impact reduced. retaining thread for RCA work and follow-ups. :thumbsup:
